body.statement: Let \(k,p,q\) be nonnegative integers and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{k\times p}\) and \(D\in\mathbb R^{k\times q}\).  Write \(U_A\) and \(U_D\) for their sets of nonzero columns, and let \(\mathscr L(A)\) be the set of laws of \(A\xi\) as the coordinates of \(\xi\) range independently over all nonconstant, non-Gaussian real laws, without centering or moment restrictions.  Then \(\mathscr L(A)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)\) if and only if there are a surjection \(f:U_A\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero real numbers \(a_i\), \(i\in U_A\), such that \(A_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for every \(i\in U_A\).  This includes \(k=0\) and zero columns.
body.proof_tex:
Assume first that \(\mathscr L(A)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)\).  Apply containment to the diagnostic source vector \(\xi^A\) from Lemma \(\texttt{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\).  Its coordinates are legal for \(\mathscr L(A)\), so there is a legal independent nonconstant non-Gaussian vector \(\eta\) with
\[
 \mathcal L(A\xi^A)=\mathcal L(D\eta).
\]
Diagnostic rigidity supplies the required surjection and nonzero proportionality scalars.

Conversely, suppose \(f\) and \((a_i)\) exist, and take an arbitrary legal source vector \(\xi\) for \(A\).  For \(j\in U_D\), define
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\xi_i.                                      \tag{10}
\]
The fibers of the surjection are disjoint and nonempty, so the variables in (10) are mutually independent.  Each summand in (10) is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  The sum cannot be constant: the support of a sum of independent random variables contains the sum of their supports, so a singleton support for the sum would force every summand support to be a singleton.  The sum also cannot be Gaussian.  If it were a nondegenerate Gaussian, Lemma \(\texttt{lem:levy-cramer-decomposition}\) would force every nonconstant summand to be Gaussian, a contradiction.  Thus every \(\eta_j\) in (10) is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  Give each invisible column \(j\notin U_D\) an arbitrary independent Bernoulli source, independent also of (10).  Then
\[
 D\eta
 =\sum_{j\in U_D}D_{:,j}\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\xi_i
 =\sum_{i\in U_A}A_{:,i}\xi_i
 =A\xi.                                                               \tag{11}
\]
Thus every law in \(\mathscr L(A)\) belongs to \(\mathscr L(D)\).  The support argument also covers \(k=0\), and empty visible sets use the unique empty surjection.  No centering, moment, boundary, or limit condition enters either direction.
